key_insight: Large language models can substantially improve plain-language adaptation of medical texts, helping make complex healthcare information easier to understand while preserving meaning.
clinical_relevance: This approach could improve patient comprehension of medical information, supporting more accessible communication in clinical and public-facing health contexts.
method: Compared prompt-based simplification across LLMs including GPT-4o-mini, Gemini-1.5-pro, and LLaMA.
Applied QLoRA finetuning to adapt models for plain language adaptation.
Used Mixture-of-Agents (MoA) to improve robustness and flexibility in simplification tasks.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a comparative analysis of prompting strategies, finetuning, and MoA across multiple LLMs, with findings indicating effective simplification performance.
watch_item: Simplified output must still preserve critical medical meaning, and model reliability may vary across prompts, datasets, and target readability levels.
paper_title: Enhancing Accessibility of Medical Texts through Large Language Model-Driven Plain Language Adaptation
